Runs a query against the store and prints the result as tab-separated columns.

The questions worth asking of a trajectory corpus are not knowable in advance, so
the schema is published and callers write their own. These views are the contract:

  v_action   session_id, agent_id, seq, ts, tool, target, outcome
  v_session  session_id, project_dir, cwd, first_seen, last_seen, closed_at, capture_build
  v_skip     session_id, agent_id, prompt_id, reason, at
  v_thought  session_id, agent_id, prompt_id, block_seq, ts, text
  v_word     session_id, agent_id, prompt_id, block_seq, ts, role, text, source, provisional, attribution

The connection is opened read-only, with query_only and ATTACH both refused, so a
query cannot write and cannot reach a second database. Underlying tables are not
the contract: query the views.

NULL prints as the word NULL, because "" and NULL are different answers.

Usage:
  telepathy sql <query> [flags]

Examples:
  telepathy sql "SELECT tool, count(*) n FROM v_action GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC"
  telepathy sql "SELECT text FROM v_thought WHERE session_id = 'abc' ORDER BY block_seq"

Flags:
  -h, --help        help for sql
      --limit int   stop after this many rows (0 for no limit); truncation is reported (default 200)

Global Flags:
      --projects string   the transcript root, which this reads and never writes (default "<CORPUS>")
      --sessions string   where the client advertises live sessions, which is the only source of liveness (default "<SESSIONS>")
      --store string      the catalogue database the hooks write and every read verb queries (default "<STORE>")
